From 6ce9efd12ae81cf46bf44eb0348594558dfbb9d2 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Tvrtko Ursulin <tvrtko.ursulin@igalia.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jul 2024 14:53:30 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] drm/v3d: Prevent out of bounds access in performance query
 extensions
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

Check that the number of perfmons userspace is passing in the copy and
reset extensions is not greater than the internal kernel storage where
the ids will be copied into.

Signed-off-by: Tvrtko Ursulin <tvrtko.ursulin@igalia.com>
Fixes: bae7cb5d6800 ("drm/v3d: Create a CPU job extension for the reset performance query job")
Cc: Maíra Canal <mcanal@igalia.com>
Cc: Iago Toral Quiroga <itoral@igalia.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # v6.8+
Reviewed-by: Iago Toral Quiroga <itoral@igalia.com>
Reviewed-by: Maíra Canal <mcanal@igalia.com>
Signed-off-by: Maíra Canal <mcanal@igalia.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20240711135340.84617-2-tursulin@igalia.com
(cherry picked from commit f32b5128d2c440368b5bf3a7a356823e235caabb)
Signed-off-by: Thomas Zimmermann <tzimmermann@suse.de>

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/v3d/v3d_submit.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/v3d/v3d_submit.c
index 88f63d526b22..263fefc1d04f 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/v3d/v3d_submit.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/v3d/v3d_submit.c
@@ -637,6 +637,9 @@ v3d_get_cpu_reset_performance_params(struct drm_file *file_priv,
 	if (copy_from_user(&reset, ext, sizeof(reset)))
 		return -EFAULT;
 
+	if (reset.nperfmons > V3D_MAX_PERFMONS)
+		return -EINVAL;
+
 	job->job_type = V3D_CPU_JOB_TYPE_RESET_PERFORMANCE_QUERY;
 
 	job->performance_query.queries = kvmalloc_array(reset.count,
@@ -708,6 +711,9 @@ v3d_get_cpu_copy_performance_query_params(struct drm_file *file_priv,
 	if (copy.pad)
 		return -EINVAL;
 
+	if (copy.nperfmons > V3D_MAX_PERFMONS)
+		return -EINVAL;
+
 	job->job_type = V3D_CPU_JOB_TYPE_COPY_PERFORMANCE_QUERY;
 
 	job->performance_query.queries = kvmalloc_array(copy.count,
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/gpu/drm/v3d/v3d_submit.c`**
   - Added a check to ensure that the number of performance monitors (`nperfmons`) provided by userspace in the `reset` structure does not exceed the maximum allowed value (`V3D_MAX_PERFMONS`). If it does, the function returns an error code `-EINVAL`.
   - Similarly, added a check for the `copy` structure to validate that `nperfmons` does not exceed `V3D_MAX_PERFMONS`, returning `-EINVAL` if the condition is violated.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in `v3d_submit.c` are related to enhancing the safety and robustness of performance query operations by preventing out-of-bounds access. The checks added for both the `reset` and `copy` performance query parameters ensure that userspace cannot request more performance monitors than the kernel can handle, thus preventing potential memory corruption or crashes. These changes are part of a bug fix that addresses an issue introduced in a previous commit, ensuring that the performance query extensions operate within safe limits.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
for (int j = 0; j < reset.nperfmons; j++) {
```
```c
for (int j = 0; j < copy.nperfmons; j++) {
```
```c
job->performance_query.queries[i].kperfmon_ids[j] = id;
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because there is no validation for the number of performance monitors (`nperfmons`) provided by userspace. This allows userspace to request more performance monitors than the kernel's internal storage can handle, leading to out-of-bounds access when the code attempts to access `kperfmon_ids` beyond its allocated size.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (reset.nperfmons > V3D_MAX_PERFMONS)
```
```c
if (copy.nperfmons > V3D_MAX_PERFMONS)
```
Reason:
These statements add validation checks to ensure that the number of performance monitors requested by userspace does not exceed the maximum allowed (`V3D_MAX_PERFMONS`). This prevents out-of-bounds access by ensuring that the kernel only processes valid requests that fit within its internal storage limits.
